cells.tense: You are standing where something small is coming up, and you can see it as it is, not as you need it to be.
cells.ask: Offer what you see plainly and let it stand next to what they think — the two views together will grow more than either alone.
cells.core:
Seeing a thing clearly before it has shown you what it will be — that is the ordinary miracle of tending. You look at the seedbed and you know what is coming up and what is not, and you do not need it to be further along than it is. That kind of attention is what makes things safe to grow near you. You are not forcing the shape of things; you are reading them, and the reading is true.

What this balance is free to feed next is another pair of eyes on the work. Say what you see and leave it beside theirs. What comes back will tell you both something neither view had alone.
cells.sheetLine: You see what is actually here, and you tend from that.
cells.verb: seeing clearly before there is anything in particular to see
cells.place: where you tend what is still growing

cells.tense: You are seeing ahead of time — what this will need, what could go wrong — and rushing to prepare for a season that has not arrived.
cells.ask: Let one thing be exactly what it is today, before you decide anything about it, and let the next moment come in its own time.
cells.core:
You can look at something small and see its whole future — what it will need, what will go wrong, where the trouble will come. That is a real gift, and in its right size it makes you the one who catches what others miss. But the looking has run ahead of the thing. You are tending a season that has not arrived, and the thing in front of you is being handled as a problem it has not become yet.

What settles this is sitting with what is here right now, with no decision attached to it. You can still see ahead. Just not today. Today the work is to be where the small thing is.
cells.sheetLine: Care has become vigilance about a future you cannot see anyway.
cells.verb: seeing clearly before there is anything in particular to see

cells.tense: You stopped looking at what was in front of you, and you are still standing where you stopped.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you are growing and give it one clear look this week — write down what you actually see, not what it is supposed to be.
cells.core:
When this is going well, you walk out and the whole bed tells you its state in one pass — what has taken, what is struggling, what needs moving. You look and you know, and your hands follow the knowing without argument. That is what kept everything alive around you.

Somewhere the looking got set down, and now you tend from memory instead of from the thing itself. The plants changed; the picture did not. What brings it back is a look you take on purpose — one honest look at one real thing, written down where you can see it. Looking is a form of choosing, and you can choose it today.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped looking at what is here, and kept tending anyway.

cells.tense: You are already seeing clearly — it is shaping the room right now — and you are calling it nothing in particular.
cells.ask: Say out loud one thing you saw about someone that you have kept to yourself — just once, without dressing it up.
cells.core:
The seeing is always on. You notice the leaf that turned, the effort that is quietly paying off, the thing someone needs before they say it — and your care follows what you noticed without any fuss. That is the whole engine of your tending, and it runs all day.

But you have not claimed it. You talk as if the noticing were just the ordinary background, as if anyone standing there would see the same. They would not. What returns it is the simplest form of the same act: one plain observation, said once, out loud. Not a report, not a conclusion. Just what you saw.
cells.sheetLine: You are seeing it clearly already. You just call it nothing.
